text:
Carmen: Quick alignment thread — we need the public changelog + sample pack for audit schema v3, plus a short ops runbook and SIEM mapping examples. Can we finalize today?
AJ: I can draft the changelog text. Do we have a canonical schema diff from runtime?
Sam: pushed v3 diff to internal repo last night. Main additions: actor.identity.type, resource.tags (array), and auth.context.kms_key_id. Fields are optional so v2 remains accepted.
Maria: For the sample pack I recommend one sample per common flow: user_login, api_key_use, model_deploy. Include side-by-side v2 -> v3 examples so customers can diff. Keep samples minimal.
Liz: Security notes: 1) kms_key_id is an identifier only, no key material leaves our KMS; 2) add a config option for pseudonymizing actor.id on ingest for customers that require it; 3) any payload >64KB in resource.metadata should be rate-limited and considered high-severity.
Pete: CS needs a short FAQ: will this break SIEM parsers? how long is compat window? sample mapping for Splunk & Logstash would be helpful.
AJ: Draft changelog blurb: "Audit events: schema v3 — richer actor and resource metadata plus KMS identifier exposure (no key material). A new RBAC scope `audit.events.read:customer` is required for private deployments; hosted customers get org-admin mapping. v2 payloads still accepted; v3 adds optional fields to improve traceability."
Maria: Draft migration checklist for customers: 1) download sample pack; 2) validate required fields; 3) update parsers to accept resource.tags[]; 4) confirm RBAC mapping for `audit.events.read:customer`; 5) decide on actor.id pseudonymization if needed.
Carmen: Sam — paste a sanitized v3 sample payload here so docs/security can sign off.
Sam: Pasting sanitized v3 example below (customers will receive real ids/timestamps):

```
{
  "event_id": "evt_20260511_0001",
  "timestamp": "2026-05-11T14:23:01Z",
  "schema_version": "v3",
  "actor": {
    "id": "usr_9a8b7c",
    "identity": { "type": "service_account", "provider": "okta" }
  },
  "action": "model.deploy",
  "resource": {
    "id": "model_abc123",
    "type": "model",
    "tags": ["production","nlp"],
    "metadata": { "version": "v1.4.2" }
  },
  "auth": {
    "method": "kms-signed",
    "context": { "kms_key_id": "key-XXXX-ABCD" }
  },
  "outcome": "success",
  "meta": { "ingest_region": "us-west-2" }
}
```

Liz: Approved sample. Add explicit note for customers: `kms_key_id` is opaque identifier; no secret material is included. Also document the pseudonymize toggle for actor.id and example regex for masking.
AJ: We should provide a compatibility fallback: ingest endpoint accepts `schema_version: v2` flag for 30 days after rollout to reduce breakage; we'll log parsing errors and return a helpful 4xx with reason. Add this to changelog.
Maria: Adding SIEM mapping examples. Quick Splunk sourcetype sample: `sourcetype=redwood:audit event_id=... action=model.deploy resource_tags="production,nlp" kms_key_id=key-XXXX-ABCD`.
Maria: Logstash grok snippet (example):

```
%{WORD:event_action} %{DATA:event_id} %{DATA:resource_tags} %{DATA:kms_key_id}
```

Maria: And a short Logstash mutate to split tags: `mutate { split => { "resource.tags" => "," } }`.
Pete: CS FAQ answers: Q: Will this break my SIEM? A: Likely not if you consume JSON fields; update parsers to handle `resource.tags` as array or comma-separated list. Q: How long is compat window? A: 30 days with `schema_version=v2` fallback.
Carmen: Ops runbook for customer reports of missing/malformed events:
- Step 1: Verify incoming request and `schema_version` header/body.
- Step 2: Check schema-service logs for validation errors (422 -> field issues).
- Step 3: If payload_size > 64KB, confirm 413 rejection and ask customer to trim resource.metadata; metric `audit_ingest.payload_size_rejected` will increment.
- Step 4: If auth mismatch, verify private deployment KMS mapping and that principal has `audit.events.read:customer`.
- Step 5: If parses fail on customer SIEM, offer sample pack and request raw event for debugging; enable `schema_version=v2` flag if needed.
- Escalation: open ticket to eng-runtime if serialization or header mismatch suspected.
Liz: Vuln triage: treat any bug that allows >64KB metadata or unbounded `resource.metadata` as P1; implement immediate rate-limiting and block.
Sam: Runtime enforcement: 64KB cap in place, will return 413 for larger payloads. Adding metric `audit_ingest.payload_size_rejected` and monitor rule `audit-ingest-error-rate > 0.5% over 5m -> page oncall`. Staging link: https://internal.redwood/dev/schemas/audit/v3 (staging) — tests green.
Maria: Docs action: I'll produce a small sample pack (v2 + v3), Splunk & Logstash snippets, and a short FAQ page. PR will be at `docs/changes/audit-v3`.
Pete: CS will prepare canned responses and a checklist to send with sample pack.
AJ: I'll polish the changelog and add the compatibility clause and runbook summary.
Carmen: Legal review required before public announcement — I'll collate drafts and send to legal once docs PR is up.
ops-bot: schema-service: scheduled staging rollout 2026-05-12T08:00:00Z, schema-version=v3, rollout=staged-by-region.
Carmen: Thanks all — please mark items done in the thread when complete. Closing when PR + changelog are live. :white_check_mark:
